strengths: Clear problem motivation with empirical evidence (context collapse in Figure 2)
Strong empirical results across multiple benchmarks with consistent improvements (+10.6% agents, +8.6% finance)
Impressive AppWorld results matching GPT-4.1 agent with smaller model; substantial efficiency gains (86.9% latency reduction)
Comprehensive evaluation including both offline and online settings, with and without labels
Practical three-component architecture (Generator/Reflector/Curator) with well-motivated design choices
Ablation studies demonstrating contribution of individual components
Detailed prompts and standard evaluation protocols support reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: Heavy reliance on Dynamic Cheatsheet; claimed innovations (delta updates, Reflector, grow-and-refine) are engineering refinements rather than algorithmic advances
Incomplete context collapse analysis: Unfair comparison with DC (not designed for incremental updates); unclear if incremental updates alone solve the problem
Critical feedback quality dependency glossed over: Performance degrades 2-7% without reliable labels (Table 2), contradicting 'self-improvement without supervision' claims for domain tasks
Limited evaluation scope: Only 2 domains (agents + finance); unclear generalization; no evaluation on QA, code, language understanding tasks
Model comparison confounds: IBM CUGA uses GPT-4.1 while ACE uses DeepSeek-V3.1; difficult to isolate ACE contribution from model capability
Cost analysis lacks rigor: Serving cost arguments rely on unverified infrastructure optimizations; no actual cost measurements provided
Unexplained empirical phenomena: Online ACE without labels sometimes exceeds offline with labels (Table 1); inconsistencies suggest uncontrolled confounds
Ablation limitations: Only on AppWorld; missing sensitivity analyses (batch size, Reflector quality, de-duplication threshold); delta updates and Reflector contributions not isolated
No statistical significance testing or confidence intervals despite modest improvements (8.6% on finance)
Code not released; specialized datasets (financial) limit reproducibility; leaderboard snapshot time-dependent

strengths: Clear problem identification with concrete examples (brevity bias, context collapse) illustrated compellingly in Figure 2
Comprehensive empirical evaluation across agent tasks and domain-specific benchmarks with strong baselines (GEPA, Dynamic Cheatsheet) and proper experimental setup
Strong practical results: 10.6% on agents, 8.6% on finance, competitive with production systems (59.5% vs IBM-CUGA 60.3%), 82.3% latency reduction and 75.1% fewer rollouts
Extensive generalization studies across 4 LLM families (DeepSeek, GPT-OSS, GPT-5.1, Llama) showing consistent gains
Thorough ablation studies (§4.6) clearly demonstrating contribution of Reflector, multi-epoch refinement, and incremental delta updates
Practical deployment insights including fine-grained cost analysis, KV cache reuse patterns (91.8% cache hit rate), and realistic serving infrastructure discussion
Reproducibility: extensive appendix with prompts, extended results, cost breakdowns, detailed hyperparameter analysis, and promised code release
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figure 3 shows actual generated content) and well-structured writing
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: three-component architecture adapted from Dynamic Cheatsheet, incremental updates similar to prior memory curation work, grow-and-refine is straightforward deduplication. Primary contribution is engineering/combination rather than novel methodology

Critical dependency on feedback quality substantially undermines the 'without labeled supervision' claim: FiNER offline drops from 78.3% (with labels) to 71.1% (without labels, only +0.4 over base); only reliable execution signals enable improvement, severely limiting applicability

Domain-specific rather than universal benefits: excellent on AppWorld (+17.1%) and Formula (+18.0%), but weak on DDXPlus (+15.0%) and BIRD-SQL (+5.1%), suggesting effectiveness varies significantly by task type

Incomplete context quality analysis: only one partial concrete example (Figure 3), no systematic evaluation of playbook coherence/consistency/redundancy, no human evaluation, no assessment of cross-task generalization

Missing or weak baselines: ICL is relatively weak; IBM-CUGA comparison acknowledged as informal reference only; no comparison with simpler structured approaches (retrieval-based context, hierarchical summaries)

No statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, significance tests, or discussion of variance across runs; hard to assess if differences are statistically significant especially for smaller improvements

Scalability questions: largest tested context ~18K tokens, maximum pruning threshold 100K tokens but no evidence method was tested at that scale; unclear how delta updates and deduplication scale to modern 100K+ token windows
Generalization concerns: Llama-3.3-70B shows much smaller gains (+2.4% on FiNER) suggesting stronger models may achieve improvements independently

Misleading framing: 'matches top-1-ranked' agent is 0.9 points behind (59.4% vs 60.3%); 'without labeled supervision' overstates applicability given need for reliable feedback; 'self-improving' oversells test-time adaptation mechanism
Limited context collapse analysis: only one concrete example from Dynamic Cheatsheet; unclear if phenomenon is method-specific or more general across adaptation approaches

strengths: Clear identification and demonstration of real problems (context collapse, brevity bias) with concrete examples and empirical evidence
Comprehensive evaluation across multiple benchmarks (agents, finance, medical, SQL) and LLM backbones with appropriate baselines and ablations
Sound technical approach with interpretable three-component architecture that directly addresses identified limitations through incremental delta updates
Strong empirical results: +10.6% average on agents, +8.6% on domain tasks; matches top production agent on AppWorld leaderboard with smaller model
Significant practical efficiency gains: 82-91% latency reduction, 75-83% reduction in rollouts/costs with detailed infrastructure analysis (KV cache reuse)
Thorough ablation studies and sensitivity analysis demonstrating each design choice contributes meaningfully; incremental updates alone provide +13.4% gain
Works without labeled supervision in agent settings by leveraging natural execution feedback (code success/failure)
Honest discussion of limitations and appropriate scope delineation; clear about when method doesn't apply
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: three-component architecture inspired by Dynamic Cheatsheet, itemized contexts similar to A-MEM; main innovation (incremental updates + grow-and-refine) is somewhat incremental

Significant dependence on feedback quality: performance drops sharply without ground-truth labels (FiNER: 78.3%→71.1%); claim about 'self-improving without supervision' overstated since execution feedback still required
Inconsistent improvements across tasks and models: gains range from +18% (Formula) to +5.1% (BIRD-SQL); Llama-70B shows only +2.4% suggesting limited scalability to weaker models
Missing technical details: semantic deduplication algorithm not described; context growth saturation not analyzed; multi-epoch learning mechanism not clearly distinguished from simple reuse
IBM-CUGA leaderboard comparison requires careful reading (footnote 1) and isn't a direct methodological baseline; abstract claims somewhat overstated

Methodological concerns: improvements could partly stem from better task reformulation via Reflector rather than pure context accumulation; risk of overfitting to training set during multi-epoch refinement not discussed
Limited scope: evaluation concentrated on two task categories (agents + domain-specific); unclear how method generalizes to translation, summarization, tasks preferring concise prompts
Cost analysis nuances: latency gains partly from fewer rollouts; KV cache benefits depend on specific infrastructure (OpenAI API); raw input tokens increase +117.4% at evaluation time (Table 14)
